title: Finite Gibbs gentle spectral-complement bridge
question: Can the finite Gibbs spectral tail from R-394 be converted into a trace-norm disturbance budget for low-energy projection, and can the Markov tail bound be composed with that budget without hiding cutoff dependence?

model.markov_composition: tau_E <= Tr(rho_W K_W)/E implies disturbance <= 2 sqrt(Tr(rho_W K_W)/E)
model.analytic_target: prove a cutoff-independent moment bound and a dimension-safe continuity transfer from the projected finite sector to QCMI/Petz data

lean_crosscheck.boundary: Lean checks the scalar square-root envelope and its monotonicity; the trace-norm gentle-measurement theorem and every uniform/QFT transfer remain numerical or open.

qft_interface.closed: On the finite declared grid, the trace-norm disturbance from replacing a Gibbs core state by its unnormalized low-energy projection is bounded by 2 sqrt(tail), and the R-394 first-moment Markov estimate supplies a composed finite bound.
qft_interface.open: The moment bound grows with cutoff in the sampled grid; no cutoff-independent tail, dimension-safe QCMI continuity, projected QCMI transfer, shell summability, common core, Cook/common-alpha, OS/KMS/GNS, gap, continuum, C6, Sector-A or Pre-A result follows.
qft_interface.tect_boundary: Auxiliary finite state-disturbance interface only; no physical-sector conclusion or production-owner transfer is supplied.

boundary: T0 claim-nonbearing finite gentle spectral-projection bridge only. It proves no cutoff-independent moment bound, dimension-safe QCMI continuity, Gibbs complement theorem, shell modulus, source/volume/shape bound, common core, beta/eta-independent topology, domain or Cook/common-alpha convergence, OS/KMS/GNS reconstruction, gap, continuum, C6, Sector-A or Pre-A result.
no_overclaim: The finite trace-norm bridge makes the missing complement error explicit and composable; it does not make the error small uniformly, and it cannot transfer QCMI or a physical gap without a dimension-safe continuity theorem and a uniform moment estimate.
